summary:
The Congenital Heart Futures Reauthorization Act of 2024 amends section 399V-2 of the Public Health Service Act, 42 U.S.C. § 280g-13, to reauthorize the national congenital heart disease research, surveillance, and awareness program and to impose new reporting and strategic-planning requirements on the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

Section 1 designates the Act’s short title as the “Congenital Heart Futures Reauthorization Act of 2024,” codified as a note to 42 U.S.C. § 201.

Section 2 amends PHSA § 399V-2 by redesignating existing subsections (f) and (g) as subsections (g) and (h), respectively, and inserting a new subsection (f), captioned “Report and Strategy.” New § 399V-2(f)(1) requires the Secretary, not later than 2 years after enactment, to submit a report to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. The report must include: a description of past and present HHS activities to increase public awareness and knowledge of congenital heart disease, including efforts addressing the lifelong needs of patients; an assessment of past and present HHS activities to increase education and training of health care providers regarding congenital heart disease, including those lifelong needs; and a description of current U.S. workforce capacity among health care providers treating adult patients living with congenital heart disease.

New § 399V-2(f)(2) requires the Secretary, not later than 1 year after submitting the report, to develop and submit to Congress a strategy to improve public awareness and knowledge and provider education and training regarding congenital heart disease. The strategy must include findings and recommendations addressing public awareness and research gaps and opportunities related to lifelong patient needs, including long-term health outcomes, quality of life, mental health, and health care utilization; shortages in the workforce treating adult congenital heart disease patients, including possible strategies to enhance fellowship training or continuing education programs; and collaboration and information dissemination among Federal agencies, providers, researchers, and patient organizations. In developing the strategy, the Secretary must consult, as appropriate, with specified stakeholder groups and relevant Federal agencies, including CDC, NIH, and HRSA.

Finally, section 2 amends redesignated § 399V-2(h) to extend the existing authorization of appropriations from fiscal years 2020 through 2024 to fiscal years 2025 through 2029. The Act authorizes appropriations but does not provide a direct appropriation.
